title: Estimating and assessing effort, risk and alternatives

videos.script: Three months, roughly. {{corridor}} That is how most estimates start, in a corridor, and it is how most of them go wrong. The number is not the problem. The problem is that it hides how much nobody knows yet. {{cone}} This lesson follows Renata through one question from Helena. How long would instant payout by Pix take? First, a range instead of a point. Three numbers for each piece of work, and what they add up to. {{pert}} Then risk. What could happen, how likely it is, how bad it would be, and who is watching it. {{grid}} Then the moves before a choice. A spike, which buys an answer with a few days of work. A table of options that includes doing nothing, because doing nothing has a cost too. {{options}} And a pre-mortem, where the team imagines the project has already failed and explains why. {{premortem}} By the end, Renata has one page. A range to plan against, the risks with names beside them, and a decision for somebody else to make.
